back: [[imp:A reduction from the invoice (net) price offered to encourage early payment.]]
It is optional – the buyer chooses whether to pay early and take the discount.
Example: terms 2/10, n/30 – 2% discount if paid within 10 days.

cards.front: How does a cash discount differ from a trade discount?
back: [[imp:Trade discount]] is off the list price and always taken; [[imp:cash discount]] is off the net price and only taken if paid early.
Trade discount is for being a retailer; cash discount is for paying quickly.
[[imp:2% cash discount if paid within 10 days of the invoice date; otherwise, the full net amount is due in 30 days.]]
[[imp:Discount and net due dates are calculated from the invoice date.]]
Example: 2/10, n/30 – discount period ends 10 days after invoice; net due in 30 days.
[[imp:The discount period starts after the end of the invoice month.]]
Example: 2/10, n/30 EOM on a July 8 invoice → discount until August 10.
[[imp:The discount period starts when the buyer receives the goods.]]
Example: 2/10, n/30 ROG – discount period begins the day the shipment arrives.
[[imp:On the net merchandise price only – after trade discounts, before freight.]]
Never apply cash discount to freight or taxes.
cards.front: On which amount is the cash discount calculated?
How do you calculate the check amount for an invoice with freight?
back: 1. Net price × cash discount rate = discount.
2. Net price – discount = discounted merchandise.
3. Discounted merchandise + freight = check amount.
[[imp:Freight is always added after the cash discount is applied.]]

cards.front: Why is freight not subject to a cash discount?
back: [[imp:Freight is the actual cost of shipping owed to a carrier; the seller simply passes it through.]]
Discounting freight would cause the seller to lose money on shipping.
[[imp:A portion of the invoice paid within the discount period.]]
The cash discount applies to the paid portion, increasing its value toward the debt.
[[imp:Credit = Partial Payment ÷ (1 – Cash Discount Rate)]]
This gives the amount of debt the payment actually covers.
Example: pay \$980, terms 2/10 → credit = 980 ÷ 0.98 = \$1,000.
cards.front: How do you calculate the credit received from a partial payment?

back: [[imp:Outstanding Balance = Previous Balance – Credit Received]]
Only applies if the partial payment is made within the discount period.
If paid after the discount date, no discount is given.
